applies_why: The judge text addresses a chain collision over Romans 1:3 and resolves it by noting the absence of an explicit textual resolution, so K-C governs that treatment.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires — (a) it forbids requiring an explicit contrary verse and requires chain-vs-chain footing; (b) it allows underdetermination because no verse explicitly resolves paternity.
why: The judge calls the Romans 1:3 paternity issue underdetermined because there is no explicit textual resolution, which is the retired stating-verse test rather than a chain-vs-chain footing decision.
